solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Store took a lot of booze back

indicators.note: back tells the solver to read the drinking word from its end to its start

parts.note: to tope is to drink heavily, so 'took a lot of booze' is toped

explanation.surface: Someone raided the shop's stock of drink and carried it off.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a warehouse or storehouse where goods are kept, so it is a store.

clue.text: One down comes from nought

definitions.meaning: down, the soft feathers, comes from waterfowl such as this bird
in cricket a batter out without scoring has made this, a score of zero

explanation.surface: A puzzling statement that something counted as one fewer has arisen from zero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One down' reads like a crossword clue number or a loss; here it is the feathers called down.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird supplies eiderdown-style feathers, and the cricket term for a zero score is the same word.

clue.text: IKEA reports wobbly reconstruction behind the curtain

indicators.note: something wobbly is unsteady and out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: News that flat-pack furniture from the Swedish store keeps falling apart and needs rebuilding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind the curtain' means behind the Iron Curtain, the Soviet bloc.
explanation.definitionFit: Perestroika was Gorbachev's programme of restructuring the Soviet economy and politics in the 1980s.

clue.text: A western island NATO mostly protects? On the contrary

definitions.text: A western island NATO mostly protects? On the contrary

indicators.note: here taken as an instruction to turn the whole construction the opposite way round, reading it backwards
one thing protecting another wraps around it, so the shortened alliance goes around the other letters
mostly means nearly all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A question about whether the Atlantic alliance defends a certain island in the west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts NATO to NAT; 'protects' wraps NAT round AWI, giving NAWIAT; 'On the contrary' reverses it. The question mark admits the island is in the east and not a NATO member.
explanation.definitionFit: Taiwan is an island state off the Chinese coast whose security is a recurring geopolitical question.

clue.text: Short time, almost too short for bike racing

parts.note: a mo is a short time, as in 'wait a mo'

indicators.note: almost means not quite the whole word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: short, as in short-tempered, means cross

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the time allowed was nearly too brief for a cycle race.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'short' is not about length but temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Motocross is cross-country racing on motorcycles over rough off-road tracks.

clue.text: Maiden bowed before sweet explorer

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
arco is the musical direction to play with the bow
Polo is a brand of mint sweet sold in Britain

explanation.surface: A young woman curtsied before a sweet-natured traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: Polo mints are British ring-shaped peppermints.
explanation.definitionFit: Marco Polo was the Venetian traveller who journeyed to China and wrote of his travels.

clue.text: Unspoken magnetic attraction keeps returning

indicators.note: returning means the hidden letters are read backwards
the two words hold the answer's letters within them, keeping them in

explanation.surface: A wordless pull between two people that keeps coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' hides TICAT inside 'magnetic attraction'; 'returning' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means understood or implied without being stated, so it is unspoken.

clue.text: Name one work by English female that's inspiring

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them
I is the Roman numeral one
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Pick out a single work written by an inspiring Englishwoman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'female that's inspiring' means a Muse, a goddess of inspiration.
explanation.definitionFit: Calliope is the Greek Muse of epic poetry, one of the goddesses who inspire artists.

clue.text: Encouragement for Ballesteros, perhaps, if his target lacks aspiration?

indicators.note: aspiration is the breathy sound of H, so the word loses that letter

parts.note: Seve Ballesteros was a golfer, whose target is the hole

explanation.surface: A Spanish golfer is cheered on when his aim lacks ambition.
explanation.walkthrough: Seve Ballesteros was a Spanish golfer, so a Spanish cheer suits him; 'aspiration' looks like ambition but means the H sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Olé is the Spanish shout of approval and encouragement, fitting a Spaniard.

clue.text: Flight tires out relative

parts.note: a flight of stairs is a set of steps

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Climbing the stairs exhausts a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepsister is a sister by a parent's remarriage, a kind of relation by marriage.

clue.text: Horror of King and Queen being infected

definitions.note: read as a noun: a being who is infected

parts.note: Carrie is a horror novel by Stephen King
R, for Regina, is the abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A dread that the royal couple have caught some disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King and Queen' suggests royals; King is the novelist Stephen King.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrier is a person or animal harbouring a disease germ, often without symptoms, and able to pass it on.

clue.text: Maybe King's or Queen's saddle on horse's back

parts.note: a col is a saddle, a low pass between mountain peaks
in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

indicators.note: the back of the word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A rider's saddle sits on the horse's back, with royalty perhaps riding.
explanation.walkthrough: King's and Queen's are colleges at Cambridge (Queens' is spelt with the apostrophe after) and Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: King's College and Queen's College are examples of university colleges.

clue.text: New air hostess jogged for fitness on transatlantic trip, perhaps

indicators.note: jogged means shaken or jolted, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A newly hired cabin attendant went running to keep fit during a long flight.
explanation.walkthrough: The trip is by sea, not by air: the hostess is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaworthiness is a vessel's fitness to sail, as needed for an ocean crossing.

clue.text: Venus usually gave tennis shot a bit of rage

indicators.note: shot here means ruined or wrecked, so these letters are scrambled
a bit of means just a small piece, the first letter

explanation.surface: Venus Williams hits a tennis stroke in anger.
explanation.walkthrough: Venus suggests the tennis player Venus Williams; here it is the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: The planet Venus is most often seen bright in the western sky after sunset, hence its name.

clue.text: Length of a light tie attracts criticism

parts.note: a tie is a game or fixture, a match
stick is informal for criticism, as in 'taking stick'

explanation.surface: A cable's measured length on a lamp, and a neckwear choice that draws complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: A match is a light for a fire, and this is its wooden length.
explanation.definitionFit: A matchstick is the thin stem of wood forming a match, used to strike a light.

clue.text: American sailors docked in Middle Eastern port

indicators.note: docked means cut short, as a tail is docked, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a ship's sailors are its crew

explanation.surface: US Navy men have tied up in a harbour in the Levant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' looks like mooring, which suits the surface, but means cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Acre is an ancient harbour city on the coast of northern Israel.

clue.text: Residents come to mind being fed pudding with spades

indicators.note: being fed means having something put into it, so the dessert goes inside

parts.note: an idea that comes to mind is said to occur
a pie is a kind of pudding, sweet or savoury
S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: Householders recall being served a dessert while gardening.
explanation.definitionFit: Occupiers are people who live in or hold a property, so they are its residents.

clue.text: Elaborate fraud attempted; Victor's taken in by it

parts.note: a con is a fraud or swindle

indicators.note: taken in by it means held inside the preceding word, so the letter goes within it

parts.note: attempted means tried
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man called Victor was duped by a swindle someone tried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' seems to mean conned, fitting the surface, but means placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrived means artificially laboured or over-worked, much like elaborate as an adjective.

clue.text: Audio equipment to bug the fifth floor?

parts.note: to bug a phone is to tap it
E is the fifth letter of the alphabet
a ship's deck is a floor

explanation.surface: Plant a listening device on the fifth storey.
explanation.walkthrough: Ships' decks are lettered A, B, C, so the fifth floor is E deck.
explanation.definitionFit: A tape deck is a machine for playing and recording audio cassettes.

clue.text: Quarter of London church during a mass contains women

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'

indicators.note: contains means holding something inside, so the women go within the mass

parts.note: a ton is a large mass

explanation.surface: In a London church parish, a service is attended by women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mass' looks like a church service but is a weight.
explanation.definitionFit: London's Chinatown, around Gerrard Street in Soho, is a district or quarter of the city.

clue.text: Fall road trip heading for red leaves

indicators.note: leaves means goes away, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: a drive is a trip by road

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An autumn drive to see the leaves turning red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall' and 'leaves' suggest autumn; both are mechanisms here.
explanation.definitionFit: To dive is to plunge or drop sharply, which is to fall.

clue.text: Slight difficulty listening to bumpkin going on

indicators.note: listening to tells us the answer is heard, not seen, as these words

parts.note: a bumpkin is a hick, a country yokel; up means going on, as in 'what's up?'

explanation.surface: A minor snag while hearing a country fellow ramble on.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiccup is informal for a minor setback or snag.

clue.text: Ray stole jewellery including diamonds for sport

parts.note: a skate is a kind of ray fish
a boa is a long scarf or stole

indicators.note: including means holding within, so the card letter goes inside

parts.note: a ring is an item of jewellery
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A man named Ray stole gems, diamonds among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a name and 'stole' like theft; they are a fish and a scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: Skateboarding, riding a board on wheels, is a recognised sport.

clue.text: Class seconds from hometime tries addition very grudgingly

indicators.note: seconds from means the second letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A pupil at the end of the school day reluctantly attempts some sums.
explanation.definitionFit: An order is a rank or category in biology and elsewhere, a class of things.

clue.text: An operating system's troubles

parts.note: an gives the article A
DOS, the disk operating system, is an early computer operating system

explanation.surface: A computer's software suffers glitches.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado is fuss or bother, so its plural means troubles or fusses.

clue.text: Rather ruins tea dunking sandwiches

indicators.note: sandwiches means holds between, so the answer is held within these words

explanation.surface: Dipping biscuits into a cuppa spoils it, as do soggy sandwiches.
explanation.definitionFit: Instead means as an alternative, as 'rather' does in 'I'd rather walk'.

clue.text: Spring ultimately comes every year

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the word's final letter is taken

parts.note: PA, for per annum, means every year

explanation.surface: Springtime arrives in the end, every year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season but is a mineral spring.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a mineral spring, or a resort built around one.

clue.text: Virginia played without Charlie after Charlie left

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

indicators.note: without means the letter is first taken out of where it sat in the word
after Charlie says the removed letter returns with the rest coming after it, so it now leads

parts.note: to have played a part is to have acted
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A woman named Virginia performed without a man called Charlie after he walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like part of the story of Charlie walking out, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To have vacated a place is to have moved out of it, that is, to have left.

clue.text: Foul dank creek completely drained

indicators.note: foul means fouled up or muddled, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A stinking, damp stream has been pumped dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Knackered is British slang for exhausted, so totally drained of energy.

clue.text: Helen's second husband runs forward in doubles

indicators.note: forward in means shifted nearer the front within the word

parts.note: doubles are pairs
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A tennis player called Helen remarried; her new partner moves up at the net in doubles.
explanation.walkthrough: Helen of Troy left Menelaus for the Trojan prince.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris, prince of Troy, carried off Helen, wife of Menelaus, effectively becoming her second husband.
